answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and no auto-renew, the first decision must keep supply flowing. The primary objective is cost reduction (finance mandate: 18% cut). Past experience shows multi-year commitments with the incumbent unlocked volume pricing (c6) and renegotiating at renewal recovered real margin (c4). The incumbent relationship is also stable and delivery has been reliable (c1), which matters given the line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer. Therefore the lowest-risk path to the 18% cost reduction is to renew with the incumbent but on renegotiated, multi-year terms that capture the volume discount and margin recovery observed in past cycles. Switching primary vendors (c2) would risk delivery stability with no buffer to absorb a transition. Adding a second source (c3) is a structural change that does not itself reduce spend and is better suited for constrained components, which is not the stated issue here. Deferring (c5) works for non-critical renewals, but this one expires in 14 days with no auto-renew — deferring would create a supply gap.
